hints: Focus on what type of reaction turns a carboxylic acid into its sodium salt, and what the other products tell you.
Remember that both carbonates and hydrogencarbonates react with acids to release bubbles of carbon dioxide gas.
Look for the reagent that neutralises the acid to give only salt and water, with no gas to be seen.
walkthrough:
**Identify the reaction type**

Propanoic acid is a carboxylic acid. To make its sodium salt, sodium propanoate, we need an acid-base neutralisation with a sodium-containing base.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COONa}$$

**Use the no gas clue**

The question says no gas is produced. This is the key filter. Acids react with carbonates and hydrogencarbonates to give salt + water + carbon dioxide gas, so those cannot be X.

**Test sodium hydroxide**

Sodium hydroxide is a strong alkali. It neutralises the acid cleanly with no gas, just salt and water.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COOH} + \text{NaOH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COONa} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Conclude the choice**

Only sodium hydroxide fits both conditions: it gives sodium propanoate as the organic product and produces no gas.

options.A: NaHCO3 does react with propanoic acid to give sodium propanoate, but it also gives water and carbon dioxide gas. The equation gives CO2 bubbles, so it fails the no gas condition.
options.B: NaOH neutralises propanoic acid in a simple acid-alkali reaction to give sodium propanoate and water only. No carbon dioxide or other gas is formed, so it matches perfectly.
options.C: Na2CO3 also reacts with propanoic acid to give sodium propanoate, but like all carbonates with acids, it releases carbon dioxide gas. This contradicts the observation of no gas.
options.D: Na2SO4 is a neutral salt, not a base. It will not neutralise propanoic acid at room temperature, so no sodium propanoate would form at all.
